subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw add LLM-driven contextual activation for group chats, and should it live in core shared activation or behind a plugin/channel API seam?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but maintainers must choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure contract, config surface, and long-term ownership for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and proof requirements before accepting code.

options.title: Narrow to ambient room events
options.body: Treat existing always-on room-event plus message-tool behavior as the supported path and document why a separate decision model is not planned yet.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API seam work
options.body: Hold core activation changes until a trusted observation or decision hook can safely support this as plugin-owned behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and proof requirements before accepting code.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history across the current activation parser, shared mention policy, and the group-gating paths involved in the decision.
